items.title: John Pizzarelli, Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I got a nice review in the Times. John Wilson came down and

ctx.x: Was it aggravating at the time?

Oh, it was just hell. I mean I was angry for the whole time, and I’d say stupid things to my father, like, “all right already.” You know I was just grinding my teeth you know. And I sang too at that time. I got a nice review in the Times. John Wilson came down and

reviewed us. But it was really hard. It’s still hard. And I used to say to him every once in a while, “could maybe you — could just call the chords out?” You know, “there’s a chord you want to hear, could you just tell me C7? That would help.” And he’d go ahhh.

items.q: no this is John Wilson in December of ’85 when he says

ctx.x: And that’s a turn off. But I also just wanted to make an observation that I like the fact that you know you only have three musicians but sometimes people don’t realize that taking out an instrument or two adds another texture to the whole affair, and you all did that.

Yeah well it’s a — that’s — everything involved in the drumless trio, which we did — actually I think when I first talked to you we had drums in the group or were just starting to have more drums. Tony Tedesco played with us for years and it was really a monetary decision to go back to the drumless group because we were going to Europe and I said well we can’t afford this but I can do it with a drumless group because it gives me another harmonic instrument, the piano. So piano, guitar and bass. And I’m used to…

Yes. And when you do that thing of the other guys drop out and it was uptempo and you’re doing this [scats] and I remember thinking, “Wow, is he going to make it?” First of all it just physically seems like a thing — I wonder if you’ve ever been doing that and you like drop a beat or add a beat?
